adaptations: Relative imports use .js suffixes for native ESM.
Tests use Vitest directly and import protocol modules from their new directory.
The default SETUP implementation identifier names @mux/moq-core. The existing error identity symbol is retained for interoperability.
Publish session extraction excludes the SPF actor and accepts explicit track properties instead of imposing the LOC microsecond timescale.
Publish protocol tests exclude media-engine integration and actor tests; raw tracks assert no implicit timescale.
SDK relay-hub test helper is derived from Video.js publish tests and adapted to local protocol imports.

The package index additionally re-exports ByteWriter, encodeKeyValuePairs and MAX_OBJECT_PROPERTIES_LENGTH so the SDK can measure encoded properties with the core's own encoder before a write starts; the protocol modules are unchanged.

The subscribe session's close sends no GOAWAY, unlike the upstream driver's best-effort GOAWAY(0): one written as the transport closes gives the peer nothing to act on and the session has no drain to offer, and the publish session already sends none (spec/behavior.md, "Relay interop deviations"; issue #128). Receiving GOAWAY is unchanged.

The publish session closes with INVALID_REQUEST_ID rather than PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when the peer reuses a request ID, and also when a peer request ID has the client's (even) parity, as draft-22 Section 6.4.2.1 requires. Tests that stand the subscribe driver in for the relay give it odd request IDs through a transport wrapper.

The subscribe session closes with INVALID_REQUEST_ID too when a server-initiated request reuses a request ID or has the client's (even) parity, checked before the request is answered, so a request the client rejects still consumes its ID (draft-22 Section 6.4.2.1).

The publish session ends each Established subscription it ends with PUBLISH_DONE (a status, and a Stream Count of the data streams opened for it) after closing that subscription's data streams, then FIN, instead of the upstream FIN alone. `openUniStream(trackAlias)` names the subscription a data stream serves, so the session can count it and reset it if still open. This needs moq-relay 0.15.4 or later (spec/behavior.md, "Relay interop deviations"; issue #132).

An orderly publish session close, after the bounded write drain, also waits (`CLOSE_END_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`, 2 s) for the peer to end its side of every request stream it is still serving before closing the transport, instead of the upstream close right after the write drain. moq-relay FINs that side only after it has read PUBLISH_DONE and finished the track; a transport closed sooner aborts the track and viewers see PUBLISH_DONE status 0 (spec/behavior.md, "Relay interop deviations"; issue #25).

The subscribe session FINs its side of a subscription's request stream once the publisher's FIN follows PUBLISH_DONE, as draft-22 Section 6.4.2.2 says a requester SHOULD, instead of the upstream driver leaving it open. A publisher closing waits for that FIN before closing the transport, so an SDK publisher closing ahead of an SDK subscriber no longer waits out the 2 s bound. A follow-up message on a request stream whose sending side has ended writes nothing (spec/behavior.md, "Relay interop deviations"; issue #142).
The package index also re-exports the types that public signatures reference, and TSDoc comments were added to exported declarations for the generated API reference (issue #179); code is unchanged.

The core speaks moq-transport draft-22 by default and draft-20 as a fallback, where the upstream snapshot speaks draft-20 only. The two differ on the wire only in the LOCATION_FILTER parameter (draft-22 Section 9.20.9: a Location Filter Type selects the fields and there is no length; draft-20 length-prefixes the fields), so the codec takes the negotiated identifier: `MOQT_PROTOCOL_IDS` lists both in preference order, each session reads `transport.protocol` through `resolveMoqtProtocol`, and every encoder and decoder that carries message parameters takes a trailing `protocol` argument that defaults to `moqt-22`. Section citations in the protocol modules follow draft-22's numbering (docs/research/moqt-22-delta.md; issue #274).
migration: Initial extraction snapshot. Video.js still contains the original modules; migrating it to this independently versioned package is a separate integration step. Do not maintain divergent protocol implementations.
